description: Section 5 (frontend): add a 'Support this work' voluntary-contribution section to every Blog article, placed AFTER the Tags nav and BEFORE the share controls, with centrally-configurable preset amounts and validated custom amount. The UI is wired to the (gated-off) BLOG_CONTRIBUTION backend from FEAT-004 but cannot complete a real charge while the gate is off; it degrades honestly when contributions are unavailable.
steps: Create a central config module src/config/contribution.ts following the src/config/share.ts precedent: export the preset amounts (49, 99, 199 rupees, expressed canonically e.g. CONTRIBUTION_PRESETS_PAISE = [4900, 9900, 19900] plus an 'Other' option), the currency ('INR'), and the min/max bounds for a validated custom amount. These presets must NOT be duplicated anywhere else - everything reads this module. Document that the SERVER (FEAT-004) is the authority on the allowed amount range; the browser value is only a request.

Create a reusable component src/components/BlogContribution.tsx: heading 'Support this work' and the message 'If this article was useful, you can make a small voluntary contribution to support more independent writing and practical guides from WECARE.DIGITAL.' (or the stated 'Found this useful?' alternative). Render the preset amount choices (from src/config/contribution.ts) plus an 'Other' custom-amount input with client-side validation against the configured bounds (validation is a UX convenience; the server re-validates authoritatively). Props: postId and slug so the contribution is attributable. Use scoped styled-jsx with a dedicated class prefix, reuse existing colours/typography/button treatment, keep accessibility (labelled inputs, focus-visible, no new h1).

Wire the contribution action to call the backend contribution-initiation endpoint (the FEAT-004 handler) exactly as the website checkout UI pattern does: send postId, slug and the chosen amount; the server returns PAYMENT_INITIATION_DISABLED (gate off, the default) or CHECKOUT_OPTIONS_READY-style browser-safe options. When disabled/unavailable, show a clear, honest non-error state (e.g. 'Contributions are not available right now.') and NEVER fabricate a success. Never treat a browser callback/query string/frontend state as proof of payment.

Insert <BlogContribution postId={...} slug={post.slug} /> into src/pages/post/[slug].tsx in the exact DOM position: AFTER the `{ post.tags && ... <nav className="tags"> ... </nav> }` block and BEFORE the `<div className="post-share" ref={ shareRef }>` block, preserving the reveal-effect sentinel (shareRef stays on .post-share). Confirm the resulting order is content -> Tags -> Contribution -> Share -> pager/related.

Guard the placement and DOM order with a vitest test (extend or follow BlogDesign.test.tsx, which already renders <BlogPostPage post={samplePost} /> with minimal props): assert the contribution block renders after the tags and before the share row, the heading/message are present, presets come from the config module, and custom-amount validation rejects out-of-range input. Add a BlogContribution.test.tsx for the component in isolation (preset rendering, validation, disabled/unavailable state renders no success).
Confirm no accessibility/structured-data regressions: the post page still has exactly one <main> and one <h1> (the contribution uses an h2/h3, not h1), and htmlcheck/typecheck guards still pass.
Commit to feature/customer-experience-upgrade with explicit-path staging only.
acceptance_criteria: Every blog article renders the 'Support this work' contribution section in the exact position: after Tags, before Share; a vitest test asserts this order and fails if the block is moved.

Preset amounts (49/99/199 + Other) come from a single central config module (src/config/contribution.ts) with no duplicated hard-coded amounts; custom amounts are validated client-side against configured bounds.
With the backend gate off (default), the UI shows an honest unavailable state and cannot complete a charge; it never fabricates success and never treats a browser signal as payment proof.
Post page still has one main and one h1; existing BlogDesign/html/type guards pass.
Full gate stays green: pytest, tsc --noEmit, vitest, npm run build.
verification: npx vitest run (BlogContribution.test.tsx + BlogDesign placement assertions pass)
npm run build (re-run once if the only failure is a transient blog 429; posts still export)
findings: DONE on branch feature/customer-experience-upgrade. PLACEMENT: inserted <BlogContribution postId={post.id} slug={post.slug} /> in src/pages/post/[slug].tsx immediately AFTER the `{post.tags && ... <nav className="tags"> ... </nav>}` block and immediately BEFORE the `<div className="post-share" ref={shareRef}>` block. Resulting DOM order is content -> Tags -> Contribution -> Share -> pager/related. shareRef was NOT moved; it stays on .post-share (the IntersectionObserver reveal sentinel). Proof of order: new vitest in BlogDesign.test.tsx ('renders the contribution block after Tags and before Share') asserts tags.compareDocumentPosition(contribution) & FOLLOWING and contribution.compareDocumentPosition(share) & FOLLOWING, so it fails if the block moves. Verified in built output: out/post/<slug>/index.html contains 'Support this work' and class="bc" (renders server-side as the default available-presets state, so static export is unaffected). post.id is the correct attributable field (PublicBlogPost.id in src/lib/public-blog.ts); both postId and slug are passed. CONFIG MODULE: created src/config/contribution.ts (mirrors src/config/share.ts precedent) exporting CONTRIBUTION_CURRENCY='INR', CONTRIBUTION_PRESETS_PAISE=[4900,9900,19900] (= ₹49/₹99/₹199, canonical integer paise), CONTRIBUTION_MIN_PAISE=1000 (₹10) / CONTRIBUTION_MAX_PAISE=10_000_000 (₹1,00,000) client-side hint bounds, plus helpers paiseToRupees/rupeesToPaise/isAllowedContributionPaise and CONTRIBUTION_PURPOSE='BLOG_CONTRIBUTION'. Header comment documents that the SERVER (FEAT-004) is authoritative on the allowed range and the browser value is only a request; presets/bounds live ONLY here (no duplicated literals - the component and both tests read this module). COMPONENT: src/components/BlogContribution.tsx, scoped styled-jsx with .bc- prefix, reuses the post page's hairline band + the site lime CTA language (#d1f470/#1a3a2a, opaque focus rings). Heading is an h2 'Support this work' (never h1), primary mandated copy used verbatim. Renders preset radios from the config + an 'Other' custom-amount input with client-side validation against the config bounds (accessible: radiogroup, labelled custom input with aria-describedby, focus-visible). HONEST DEGRADATION: the client POSTs {purpose:'BLOG_CONTRIBUTION', postId, slug, amountPaise, currency} to `${NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE||'https://wecare.digital/api'}/ecommerce/contribution` ONLY on a user click (never at render/prerender, so the static build is safe). It branches on the website-checkout contract documented in amplify/functions/ecommerce/checkout/handler.py: CHECKOUT_OPTIONS_READY -> phase 'ready' ('Opening a secure payment…', NOT a receipt - actual Razorpay open+verify is FEAT-004); PAYMENT_INITIATION_DISABLED (the default gate) / CHECKOUT_REJECTED / CHECKOUT_AMBIGUOUS / unknown state / non-OK (incl. 404 missing endpoint) / network failure all -> phase 'unavailable' with the single honest message 'Contributions are not available right now.' Never fabricates success; never treats a query string, browser callback, frontend state or bare signature as payment proof. Invalid/out-of-range/non-numeric custom amounts set phase 'invalid' and do NOT fetch. TESTS: BlogContribution.test.tsx (12 tests: presets from config, h2/copy, validation rejects out-of-range + non-numeric without fetching, correct POST body, honest unavailable on disabled/404/network/rejected/ambiguous/unknown, ready-is-not-a-receipt, no fetch at render). BlogDesign.test.tsx extended with 3 post-page tests (DOM order, heading+message+single-h1, presets-from-config). GATE COUNTS (true, post-change): tsc --noEmit exit 0; vitest 729 passed / 53 files (baseline 714/52, +15 new); npm run build exit 0 with 1409 sitemap URLs (1321 blog posts) and all 1321 post pages exported to out/post. The FIRST build attempt died on the documented transient upstream blog 429 at /post/<slug>; re-run succeeded cleanly (sitemap+llms output confirms completion). pytest NOT re-run as no backend file was touched (backend remains at its green baseline). No edits to Sections 1/2/4 files, terms.ts or privacy.ts.
